correctness.rationale: Invariance of the Lie derivatives of x, y, z, \(x^3/3\) and yz gives zero means for y and z, \(\int x^2=2c^2\), \(\int x^2y=0\), and then \(\int z^2=\int y^2\). Zero common derivative energy forces y=z=0 on the invariant support and hence support on the two equilibria. For a nonconstant periodic orbit, y has zero time mean and z is its derivative, so Wirtinger plus equality of the two energies gives \(P\ge2\pi\). Equality makes y a first harmonic; substituting \(x=m+A\sin t\) into the third equation forces the \(\sin^2t\) coefficient \(-A^2/2\) to vanish, contradicting nonconstancy. Finally the exact average of \(x^2\) and continuity force the two absolute-value threshold crossings. Fresh symbolic reconstruction independently reproduced all Lie-derivative identities.

value.rationale: The Michelson flow is a classical recurrent/chaotic model whose literature centers on periodic branches and connecting geometry. Exact stationary moment identities valid for every compact invariant measure and a universal strict lower period bound constrain all such recurrent dynamics at once and provide a natural analytic benchmark.
residual_risks: An unindexed older period estimate may use a different scalar third-order formulation.
The generalized-Michelson literature may contain related local estimates that do not appear in the bounded searches.

final_claim: For the Michelson flow \(\dot x=y\), \(\dot y=z\), \(\dot z=c^2-y-x^2/2\) with \(c>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability satisfies \(\int x^2=2c^2\) and \(\int y^2=\int z^2\), with positive derivative energy off the two equilibria; every nonconstant periodic orbit has least period strictly greater than \(2\pi\) and attains points with both \(|x|<\sqrt2c\) and \(|x|>\sqrt2c\).
limitations: The theorem does not establish existence, uniqueness, stability, entropy, or a quantitative positive gap above \(2\pi\).
The invariant-measure statement assumes compact support.
